name: social security number (employee identification number)
issuer: the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA)
note: Marshall Islands's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: the RMI issues no TINs; every employee working there must apply to the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA) for a personal social security (employee identification) number, which identifies taxpayers: 04, a dash and six digits (04 is the code the United States assigned the freely associated states). Read as given on starting work, to workers; `needed` is work and tax. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Marshall Islands: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Every employee working in the RMI is required to apply to MISSA for a personal social security number (SSN) or employee identification number. ... The employee identification number always starts with “04” and always ends with a six digit number with a dash sign in between the numbers, e.g., 04-086123.
